title: 1971 AHSME Problem 27
statement: A box contains chips, each of which is red, white, or blue. The number of blue chips is at least half the number of white chips and at most one-third the number of red chips. The number which are white or blue is at least \(55.\) The minimum number of red chips is:

solutions.text:
Let the counts be \(r,w,b.\) The conditions give \[ \begin{gathered} w\le2b,\\ r\ge3b,\\ w+b\ge55. \end{gathered} \] Hence \(3b\ge w+b\ge55,\) so \(b\ge19\) and \(r\ge57.\) Equality is possible with \((w,b,r)=(36,19,57),\) so the minimum is \(57.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let the counts be \(r,w,b\) and translate every condition into an inequality
From \(w\le2b\) and \(w+b\ge55\), find the least possible integer \(b\)
